messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Two knowledge-graph relations extracted from drug information texts are given below. Decide whether they express the same meaning with the same subject/object direction, so that they can be merged into one relation without losing information.

Relation A: 'occur with or without' defined as 'The subject condition or phenomenon can happen in the presence or absence of the factor or intervention specified by the object entity.'
Example triple with A: ["nicotine withdrawal symptoms", "occur with or without", "using medication such as bupropion"]
Relation B: 'may cause' defined as 'The subject action or condition can lead to or contribute to the development of the medical condition or effect specified by the object entity.'
Example triple with B: ["smoking cessation", "may cause", "new or worsening mental health problems"]

Do relations A and B express the same meaning, so that every triple using A could use B instead without changing the fact it states? Answer with only "yes" or "no".
Answer:
